summary: Propagate one neutral distribution generation in space with dimensionless axial nodes and normalized inverse-length transport/source coefficients.

capability: Propagate one neutral distribution generation in space with dimensionless axial nodes and normalized inverse-length transport/source coefficients.
operation: propagate one neutral generation along both velocity branches
vx, Ak/Bk/Fk/Ck/Dk/Gk, generation_kind, incoming_boundary or scattered_source -> generation distribution
discovery.model: Bidirectional recurrence using caller-provided transport coefficients; normalized spatial transport with u=v/Vth and inverse-length collision coefficients
discovery.geometry: one spatial dimension, two velocity branches; velocity axes are dimensionless u=v/Vth on one common caller normalization
discovery.boundary: vx one-dimensional with both positive and negative branches; six coefficient fields finite aligned 3-D; generation_kind in {first_flight, scattered}; first_flight requires incoming_boundary; scattered requires scattered_source_distribution; nx must be at least one (a zero-node spatial axis fails closed with a named ValueError rather than a raw IndexError)

identity.relation: bidirectional spatial propagation of one neutral generation using the supplied transport coefficients
identity.direction: vx, Ak/Bk/Fk/Ck/Dk/Gk, generation_kind, incoming_boundary or scattered_source -> generation distribution
identity.definition: first_flight: forward from boundary on positive vx using Fk as source term, backward on negative vx using Gk as source term; scattered: forward on positive vx using Bk as source coefficient, backward on negative vx using Dk as source coefficient.
identity.model: Bidirectional recurrence using caller-provided transport coefficients
identity.geometry: one spatial dimension, two velocity branches
identity.coordinates: vx is dimensionless u_x=v_x/Vth; generation and incoming boundary are distribution densities F in m^-3; Ak/Ck are dimensionless, Bk/Dk are m, Fk/Gk are F and scattered_source_distribution is F/m.
identity.boundary: vx one-dimensional with both positive and negative branches; six coefficient fields finite aligned 3-D; generation_kind in {first_flight, scattered}; first_flight requires incoming_boundary; scattered requires scattered_source_distribution; nx must be at least one (a zero-node spatial axis fails closed with a named ValueError rather than a raw IndexError)
assumptions: The supplied Ak/Bk/Fk/Ck/Dk/Gk fields define the recurrence; this callable does not choose a spatial discretization or enforce positivity.
The two generation kinds are mutually exclusive: first_flight uses incoming_boundary, scattered uses scattered_source_distribution.

The incoming_boundary applies only to the positive-vx branch (the forward propagation entry point); the negative-vx branch starts from zero at the right boundary (generation[:, negative, x.size-1] remains zero).
The dimensionless vx axis and the six transport coefficients must use one common Vth normalization; this propagation does not multiply velocities or sources by Vth.
The vx axis must be finite (NaN/inf rejected); a NaN vx node would otherwise be silently left zero.
SciRel rejects boolean, string and complex coercions and any non-finite generation produced from finite inputs.

first_flight uses Fk as the forward source term; scattered uses Bk (positive) and Dk (negative) as source coefficients. The two kinds are distinguished by which coefficient enters the recurrence, confirmed by a regression test.
The generation[:, positive, 0] indexing would raise a raw IndexError for nx=0 with an empty axis; this asset fail-closes with a named ValueError requiring nx >= 1.

The public transport convention is u=v/Vth on one caller-selected thermal-speed scale: alpha=nu/Vth has units m^-1, F integrates over normalized velocity volume to number density in m^-3, and every spatial source coefficient is Q/Vth in F/m. Physical rates in s^-1 must be divided by that same Vth before this spatial operator; no automatic conversion is performed.

inputs.name: vx
inputs.constraints: Finite one-dimensional with both positive and negative branches.

inputs.name: incoming_boundary
inputs.constraints: Required for first_flight; must be finite and aligned; must be None for scattered.

inputs.name: scattered_source_distribution
inputs.constraints: Required for scattered; must be finite and aligned; must be None for first_flight.

preconditions: Six finite aligned coefficient fields; vx with both branches; exactly one of incoming_boundary (first_flight) or scattered_source_distribution (scattered).
Use one common Vth for normalized velocity nodes, inverse-length collision coefficients and spatial source coefficients; the callable performs no implicit unit conversion.
supported: First-flight and scattered neutral generation propagation for H and H2 transport.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when vx lacks branches, coefficient fields are not finite aligned 3-D, generation_kind is invalid, or the wrong source/boundary is supplied.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if finite inputs overflow to a non-finite generation.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no result.

python.signature: propagate_neutral_generation(vx, Ak, Bk, Fk, Ck, Dk, Gk, generation_kind, incoming_boundary=None, scattered_source_distribution=None)

example.description: Propagate a first-flight generation from a uniform boundary.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic import assemble_neutral_upwind_transport_coefficients, propagate_neutral_generation
x = np.linspace(0, 1, 3)
vx = np.array([-1.0, 1.0])
alpha = np.ones((2, 2, 3))
source = np.ones((2, 2, 3))
r = assemble_neutral_upwind_transport_coefficients(x, vx, alpha, source)
boundary = np.ones((2, 2))
gen = propagate_neutral_generation(vx, r['Ak'], r['Bk'], r['Fk'], r['Ck'], r['Dk'], r['Gk'], generation_kind='first_flight', incoming_boundary=boundary)
assert gen.shape == (2, 2, 3)
assert np.all(np.isfinite(gen))
example.expected: The first-flight example returned a finite generation array of shape (2, 2, 3); the positive and negative velocity branches were propagated separately.

scope: Direct tests bind both generation kinds, Fk/Gk versus Bk/Dk source use, positive-only incoming boundary, signed boundary cells, zero-node rejection and finite-output failure semantics.
The cross-domain tests compare propagated physical attenuation against an analytic characteristic and preserve a prescribed source/loss equilibrium using one common Vth normalization.
The contract example covers one bounded representative call; numerical checks do not establish external physical validation or full-domain applicability.
